Desolate

/DESS-uh-lit/ - the stress falls on DESS · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Desolate means deserted, dreary, and lifeless.

The moor above the tree line is desolate even in June — wind, peat, and a single fence post that lost its fence.

Worked Example

The shore town's winter population fits in one school gym; its July crowds fill a mile of sand. The writer who stayed through her first winter learned the word on an afternoon walk: street after street of shuttered arcades and taffy stands, traffic lights blinking yellow for nobody, her own boot prints the only ones from the pier to the dunes. Not one thing was broken or amiss — the place was simply waiting, and the waiting had emptied it.

Desolate is the exact word for that walk, because it means deserted, dreary, and lifeless — three losses stacked in one adjective. Empty is a headcount; bleak is a sky. Desolate is what a place becomes when the people, the cheer, and the movement have all gone at once.

How Desolate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

bleak: gray and unpromising — weather, moods, prospects

forsaken: left behind by the people it needed

Antonyms

bustling

bustling: crowded with comings and goings

inviting

inviting: asks you to stay a while

How Strong Is It? — empty → deserted → desolate

empty vs. desolate

empty vs. desolate: Empty is a fact about right now — the gym at six in the morning is empty and perfectly fine.

deserted vs. desolate

deserted vs. desolate: Deserted goes further than empty — the people who belonged there have gone; desolate claims the most: emptied of life and cheer alike, with no sign anyone is coming back.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of desolate.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: completely

Root — sol-

Root — sol-: alone (Latin solus)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: made

Put it together

Put it together: De- (completely) + sol- (alone) + -ate = made completely alone. Latin desolare was "to leave utterly alone," and solus — alone — is the beating heart of it: the same root sits in solo and solitude. A desolate place is a place left utterly by itself.

Use the root in a new word: solo

Use the root in a new word: solo: A solo flight is flown alone — sol- with the loneliness turned into independence.

Word Choice

literary / atmospheric

Desolate is for places and, by extension, seasons and moods — it stacks three losses (people, cheer, life) into one word. Empty and deserted merely count heads; bleak paints the weather. Keep it beside this unit's despondent with the line clear: a desolate coast, a despondent castaway — the place is desolate, the person despondent.
